pageProps.title: The Three-Body Problem 3: Death's End
pageProps.review: The third volume of Liu Cixin's 'Three-Body' series maximizes hard sci-fi imagination regarding the nature of the universe and dimensions, marking a grand conclusion to the cosmic epic where human greed and ideals collide.
pageProps.content:
## Review In ```Death's End```, the author employs his imagination and scientific knowledge to explore the very nature of the ```universe```—pure hard sci-fi. This series features a lot of talk about dimensions. I tried to visualize everything at first, but eventually, I gave up trying to imagine it all.
The same human greed and arrogance seen in the second book reappears in this one.
I really didn't like the female protagonist. She's too idealistic and naive. She couldn't distinguish between ideals and reality, and the consequences were disastrous.
Personally, I felt the story could have ended with The Dark Forest. However, I suppose this volume was necessary for a truly complete conclusion.
